title: Boundary quenches in (1+1)-dimensional conformal field theory
authors: Michele Fossati, Colin Rylands, Eytan Grosfeld, Eran Sela, Pasquale Calabrese
abstract: We investigate a class of local quantum quenches in which the conformal boundary condition of a (1+1)-dimensional conformal field theory is abruptly changed. We derive a remarkably simple and universal expression for the time evolution of one-point functions on the half-line. This result provides a direct description of the propagation of the disturbance generated by the quench and, in turn, allows us to determine the dynamics of bipartite entanglement for subsystems adjacent to the boundary. We show that, once the subsystem becomes fully causally connected to the quench event, the entanglement entropy undergoes a sharp finite jump whose magnitude is universally given by the logarithm of the ratio of the boundary g-factors associated with the initial and final boundary conditions. We benchmark these analytical predictions against Matrix Product State simulations of the critical Ising spin chain, finding excellent agreement. The numerical analysis further allows us to investigate the time evolution of the spin-flip entanglement asymmetry, revealing how the symmetry-breaking perturbation emitted from the boundary propagates through the system. Our results uncover universal dynamical signatures of boundary quenches and establish a direct connection between nonequilibrium entanglement dynamics and boundary critical phenomena.
summary: This paper analyzes how local perturbations affect a 1+1 dimensional CFT when its boundary conditions are suddenly changed. The authors derive universal analytical results showing that the entanglement entropy jumps by $\log(g_b/g_a)$ at the quench front. By comparing these predictions with MPS simulations of the Ising model, they establish a direct link between non-equilibrium entanglement dynamics and boundary critical physics.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics resulting from abruptly changing the boundary conditions of a (1+1)-dimensional Conformal Field Theory (CFT). This addresses how local perturbations propagate across the system's boundary.
main_result: The entanglement entropy undergoes a sharp, universal finite jump of magnitude $\log(g_b/g_a)$ when the subsystem becomes causally connected to the quench event. The time evolution of one-point functions also exhibits simple, universal behavior.
method: The authors use analytical derivations based on mapping correlation functions and entanglement entropy calculations onto ratios of partition functions in replicated CFT geometries. These predictions are rigorously benchmarked against Matrix Product State (MPS) simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a (1+1)-dimensional CFT defined on a half-line, initially prepared in a ground state with boundary condition $a$, and then quenched to a final boundary condition $b$. The critical Ising spin chain serves as the primary physical realization used for numerical benchmarking.

important_parameters: The boundary g-factors ($g_a, g_b$), the quench time/distance relative to light-cone structure, and the limit $\epsilon 	o 0$ for analytic continuation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a simple boundary changing operator ($\hat{\phi}$) and relies on mapping non-equilibrium dynamics to ratios of partition functions in CFTs.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first deriving analytical expressions for one-point functions in the semi-infinite geometry under boundary quenches. It then extends this analysis to calculate the time evolution of entanglement entropy using Rényi formalism, culminating in numerical verification against MPS simulations for the Ising model.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical framework connecting non-equilibrium quantum dynamics (quenches) directly to fundamental concepts like boundary critical phenomena and entanglement structure, which has implications for understanding open quantum systems.
